candidates.title: Epic: GitHub-native Coding Agent Framework vNext
candidates.body:
## Objective
Evolve Cezar Factory into a **GitHub-native coding-agent execution platform**, not a generic agent builder. Establish durable provenance, end-to-end traces, objective verification, evidence-backed memory, and measured model efficiency while preserving existing Cezar scheduling and agent CLIs.

## Principles
- GitHub issue → bounded coding attempt → validation → reviewable PR is the primary workflow.
- Local compute only; **no GitHub Actions compute**. Preserve dev/stable release safeguards.
- Existing work remains authoritative: unified verification #47; findings #52; Hindsight #55; bounded repair #105; routing/capacity #89–#94; worker isolation #112–#113; release delivery #60.
- Separate control plane, execution plane, and evidence plane.
- Deterministic processing first; no unbounded agent loops, generic graphs, or self-grading.
- Privacy by default; immutable evidence and independently enforced policy.

## Phasing
**P1: contracts, event ledger, tracing, run explorer** (after current execution basics stabilize).
**P2: lifecycle/recovery, evidence manifests, security, acceptance links**.
**P3: memory provenance and analysis of reliability**.
**P4: model evaluation and routing analytics**.

## Definition of done
A GitHub issue is traceable end-to-end through scheduler, agent, worker, validation and PR, with reconstructible state, evidence links, accurate unknown/untested statuses, bounded failure recovery and meaningful reliability measures.

## Existing related work
#47 #49 #50 #52 #55 #57 #60 #64 #89 #90 #91 #92 #93 #94 #99 #100 #101 #102 #103 #104 #105 #106 #107 #108 #109 #112 #113.
No replacement of those issues; coordinate contracts and avoid duplicate implementation.

## Linked implementation issues
- [ ] #126 — P1 · contract (start here)
- [ ] #127 — P1 · event ledger; depends #126
- [ ] #128 — P1 · OTel; depends #126
- [ ] #129 — P1 · self-hosted Langfuse trace viewer and collector; depends #128
- [ ] #130 — P2 · evidence; depends #126 #127
- [ ] #131 — P2 · lifecycle; depends #126 #127
- [ ] #132 — P2 · acceptance evidence; depends #130
- [ ] #133 — P2 · security; depends #126 #130
- [ ] #134 — P3 · memory; depends #130 #52 #55
- [ ] #135 — P3 · UI; depends #127 #128 #130
- [ ] #136 — P3 · analytics; depends #127 #52
- [ ] #137 — P4 · model evaluation; depends #136 #89–#94

**Suggested order:** #126 → #127/#128 → #129 → #130/#131/#133 → #132 → #134/#135/#136 → #137. Existing foundational verification and routing tasks remain separate and authoritative.

## Observability technology decision — 2026-10-29
**Selected platform: Langfuse** (replaces the earlier Phoenix evaluation direction). Use OpenTelemetry as the vendor-neutral instrumentation standard and send privacy-filtered traces to self-hosted Langfuse. Langfuse is the trace/evaluation UI, **not** the authoritative coding-run event ledger (#127) or engineering memory (#55/#134). Keep provider configuration replaceable, but do not schedule a Phoenix-vs-Langfuse comparison. Follow #129 for Podman-friendly deployment, capacity/retention/security and collector integration. Relevant work: #128 #129 #135 #137.

candidates.title: Architecture: versioned coding run, attempt, event and evidence contracts
candidates.body:
Parent: #125. Phase P1.
## Scope
- ADR for GitHub issue/PR–centric workflow; define run ID, attempt ID, event ID, causation/correlation IDs, schema versions and state transitions.
- Define control/execution/evidence responsibility boundaries and event taxonomy (claim, prepare, context, implement, validate, repair, deliver, learn).
- Define source issue revision, base SHA, PR, worker, agent adapter, model/subscription, prompt/skill hash, validation IDs, artifact references.
- Define explicit unknown/unavailable values, attempt lineage and correlation with existing verification contract #49 and incident ledger #52.
- Versioning/compatibility plan; no generic agent DAG framework.
## Acceptance
Schema fixtures, ADR, migration strategy and contract tests demonstrate one complete GitHub issue lifecycle and forward-compatible readers.
## Dependencies
Existing #49 and #94; unblocks event ledger and observability.

## Tracking
- Parent: #125
- Dependencies/related: See epic #125
- Local-first execution only; no GitHub Actions compute.

candidates.title: Execution ledger: append-only events, run projections and crash-safe recovery
candidates.body:
Parent: #125. Phase P1.
## Scope
- Append-only durable execution events (PostgreSQL preferred; assess existing Cezar persistence first to avoid dual stores).
- Atomic run state projection plus event append; idempotent consumer/handler keys, durable claims/leases and recovery after interrupted workers.
- Distinguish trace sampling/retention from audit retention; expose pagination and query interfaces.
- Side-effect dedupe before GitHub PR creation/updates, branch mutation and retries; crash/restart and replay tests.
- Separate **execution** event stream from verification findings #52 and release incidents #68, with shared IDs/query boundaries rather than duplicating ledgers.
## Acceptance
Worker/scheduler crash tests retain complete event history; replay rebuilds projections and never duplicates a PR.
## Depends on
P1 execution contract; integrate #94 #52 #68.

## Tracking
- Parent: #125
- Dependencies/related: #126
- Local-first execution only; no GitHub Actions compute.
